issues.failure_explanation: The proof identifies sigma_min(I⊗A + A⊗I) with 2 sigma_min(A). This identity is false for nonnormal A. For A = [[-0.1,1],[0,-0.1]], sigma_min(A) ≈ 0.00995, but L = I⊗A + A⊗I has sigma_min(L) ≈ 0.0039. Taking E = [[-250,-25],[-25,-5]] gives R = A E + E A^T = [[0,0],[0,1]], so ||E||_2 ≈ 252.5 while ||R||_F/(2 sigma_min(A)) ≈ 50.25, violating the claimed bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 2 sigma_min(A) by sigma_min(I⊗A + A⊗I) or another valid lower bound for the Kronecker operator and propagate through teo1; this may require a new efficient estimate of that singular value.
issues.overall_effect: The certified Lyapunov/GLE error bounds (prop1, teo1) and stopping criteria based on them are invalid; the guarantee ||X - tildeX||_2 ≤ tol is not established, and numerical results relying on this certification are unreliable.
issues.title: False Lyapunov residual error bound via incorrect sigma-min identity
issues.why_classification: The central efficient error-certification guarantee is false; a correct bound requires a different, potentially expensive quantity, materially worsening the advertised complexity/guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds μ w^T A^T w by -μ sigma_min(A)||w||^2. Dissipativity only gives w^T A^T w ≤ lambda_max((A+A^T)/2)||w||^2, and -lambda_max((A+A^T)/2) can be much smaller than sigma_min(A). Counterexample: A_1 = -I + 10J, X = I, B_1 = 0, with additional modes N_i = sqrt(2/3) I so X solves the GLE and all LMIs hold. Then kappa(A_1)=1, tildeX = diag(0,2), ||X - tildeX||=1, so μ=1 satisfies the theorem condition. But hatX = diag(1,3) gives A_1 hatX + hatX A_1^T = [[-2,20],[20,-6]], which has a positive eigenvalue, so the LMI fails.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the kappa(A_j) factor by sigma_1(A_j)/(-lambda_max((A_j+A_j^T)/2)) or another dissipativity margin in the μ condition and propagate it.
issues.overall_effect: The LMI-preservation theorem and the subsequent choice μ = tol max_j kappa(A_j) are invalid; the claimed perturbation may fail to make the approximate Gramian satisfy the LMI, so the stability/error guarantees in that subsection are not established.
issues.title: False LMI-preservation perturbation condition in teo4
issues.why_classification: The core perturbation idea can be repaired locally, but the advertised kappa-based condition and sharpness are lost; μ may be much larger.

issues.failure_explanation: The observability matrix is defined with the wrong transpose and wrong dimensions: barC_j barC_j^T is p×p, not r×r, and the second term should be Sigma_j barA_j, not Sigma_j barA_j^T. The proof actually uses barA_j^T Sigma_j + Sigma_j barA_j + barC_j^T barC_j. Also H_o is defined using M_c instead of M_o. Hence the stated lemma does not define the quantity it proves.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct M_o to barA_j^T Sigma_j + Sigma_j barA_j + barC_j^T barC_j and use M_o in H_o.
issues.overall_effect: The error bound in teo5 and its use in teo6 rely on an incorrect observability term, so the stated PBR error estimate is not the proved one.
issues.title: Incorrect observability matrices in teo5 error bound
issues.why_classification: The proof already uses the corrected formulas; the repair is local and preserves the result.

issues.failure_explanation: The terms H^{1/2}H(H) and -G^{1/2}H(-G) are not well-defined real quantities when H<0 or G<0. From teo5 the contribution is -G, so when G<0 the subadditivity step should add sqrt(-G), not subtract sqrt(G). The correct expression uses positive parts, e.g. sqrt(max(H,0)) and +sqrt(max(-G,0)).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use positive-part expressions: sqrt(max(H_{c,o},0)) and +sqrt(max(-G_{c,o},0)) with appropriate Heaviside indicators.
issues.overall_effect: The main PBR error bound teo6 is ill-defined as a real inequality; it can involve square roots of negative numbers or have the wrong sign.
issues.title: Ill-defined Heaviside square-root terms in teo6
issues.why_classification: The correction is a local algebraic/sign fix; the intended bound survives.

issues.failure_explanation: The definition s_k := sum_{k=r}^{tilde n} m_k is self-referential, does not depend on the summation index, and leaves s_{tilde n+1} undefined, although the bound uses H(s_{k+1},s_k) and tilde sigma_{s_k}. It should be a cumulative sum of multiplicities, and the first term should use tilde sigma_k or indices adjusted consistently.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define cumulative dimensions s_k consistently, e.g. s_k = r + sum_{i=r+1}^k m_i with s_{tilde n+1}=n, and replace tilde sigma_{s_k} by the intended tilde sigma_k or adjust indices.
issues.overall_effect: The summation and arguments in teo6 are not well-defined, so the theorem is not a precise mathematical statement.
issues.title: Self-referential and inconsistent s_k indexing in teo6
issues.why_classification: This is a local index/notation repair; the intended structure is clear.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims A1 and A2 are normal. From the source definitions, for n=2, A1 = [[-1,0],[0.5,-1]] is not normal because A1 A1^T != A1^T A1; A2 = [[-2,-0.2],[0.8,-2]] is also not normal. The example does satisfy dissipativity directly, but not for the stated reason.

failure_location.quote: Moreover, both $\fA_1$ and $\fA_2$ are normal matrices, so the hypothesis of \Cref{teo4} holds.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the normality claim and verify dissipativity directly, or choose normal matrices.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical validation of teo4 contains a false statement about the example; the example is not normal, though it does satisfy the actual dissipativity hypothesis.
issues.title: False normality claim for synthetic example matrices
issues.why_classification: It affects only the explanatory validation, not the formal results.
